notes.summary: An antonym is a word with the opposite meaning. SSC gives a word (alone or in a sentence) and asks for its opposite. The most common mistake is choosing the synonym by habit — always remind yourself you want the opposite.

concepts.title: Opposite, same part of speech
concepts.body: The antonym of an adjective is an adjective: generous ↔ stingy. The antonym of a verb is a verb: expand ↔ contract.

concepts.title: Prefix antonyms
concepts.body: Some antonyms are formed with prefixes: un-, in-, im-, il-, ir-, dis-, mis-. legal ↔ illegal, regular ↔ irregular, honest ↔ dishonest. But options may also give a different root word with the opposite meaning.

concepts.title: Degree matters
concepts.body: Pick the direct opposite, not a weaker related idea. The antonym of ancient is modern, not young.

varieties.name: Direct word
varieties.how: Find the meaning first, then look for the option that means its opposite. Strike out the synonym trap.

varieties.name: Word in a sentence
varieties.how: Decide the meaning in that sentence, then choose its opposite.

tips: Write 'OPP' in your rough sheet as a reminder while solving antonym questions.
Learn antonym pairs together: affluent ↔ indigent, verbose ↔ concise.
If two options are synonyms of the given word, both are wrong.
traps: The synonym is almost always present among the options.
Prefix forms can mislead: inflammable means easily set on fire, the same as flammable, not its opposite.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.
Generous
questions.solution: Generous = willing to give. Opposite = unwilling to spend or give = Stingy. Liberal and Kind are near-synonyms.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.
Expand

Select the most appropriate antonym of the bold word.
His speech was so verbose that half the audience fell asleep.
questions.solution: Verbose = using more words than needed. Opposite = Concise (brief and clear). Wordy is the synonym trap.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.
Affluent
questions.solution: Affluent = rich. Opposite = Indigent (very poor). Fluent is a look-alike trap.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the bold word.
The manager gave a tacit approval to the plan by simply nodding.
questions.solution: Tacit = understood without being stated. Opposite = Explicit (stated clearly). Silent and Implied are synonyms.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.
Ameliorate
questions.solution: Ameliorate = make a bad situation better. Opposite = Aggravate (make worse). Improve, Alleviate, Amend are all close in meaning to ameliorate.
